chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whatever increases upon the fist, so it is in the Fire – meaning the beard.

key_terms.الْقَبْضَةِ: The fist (specifically a closed fist used as a measure)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the length of the beard in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific measurement for trimming the beard, defining the permissible length as no more than the span of a closed fist (qabdah). In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary textual basis for the recommendation (mustahabb) or obligation (wajib, depending on the school of thought) of maintaining a beard while keeping it neat, linking physical grooming to spiritual purity and distinctiveness from other groups.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from the one who informed him, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Whatever increases upon the fist, so it is in the Fire’ – meaning the beard’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from those who narrated to him has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Whatever of beard exceeds the fist is in the fire.’”
